Issued at 210 AM CDT Wed Oct 14 2026

Though Tonight:

Early morning GOES-19 water vapor imagery depicts a (nearly 
cut-off) upper-level trough propagating atop the Four Corners 
region. Several clusters of showers and thunderstorms are 
ongoing ahead of the trough associated with several upper- 
level vorticity maxima propagating atop an elongated baroclinic 
zone draped from the Southern Plains through the Lower Great 
Lakes. Locally, have been monitoring scattered storms across the
area though relatively meager instability is maintaining a 
relatively generic quality intensity in spite of an otherwise 
favorable shear profile for organized convection. Meanwhile, a 
sprawling 1020mb+ surface high pressure system is building into 
the northern Plains, ahead of which an expansive region of low-
level stratus is oozing southward through the Upper Midwest. 

After daybreak, the aforementioned surface high pressure system
will shift eastward toward the Upper Great Lakes leading to an 
increase in northeasterly flow across northern Illinois and 
northwestern Indiana. As a result, the low-level baroclinic zone
in which showers and thunderstorms are ongoing will shift 
southward with time. Low-level onshore flow within a marginally
unstable lake effect regime beneath a stout low-level inversion
will reinforce low-level stratus through the morning and early 
afternoon hours, leading to a gray start to the day. Cannot rule
out a few instances of sprinkles or drizzle near Lake Michigan 
or near US-24 (closer to the low-level baroclinic zone), so will
maintain low-end PoPs (10-20% chances) generally east of I-39 
and south of I-80 through the day. The high temperature forecast
will hinge entirely on whether or not stratus is able to clear 
by early this afternoon, with high res guidance providing an 
affirmative "no." As such guidance can sometimes be too
aggressive with stratus, will take the middle ground and advertise
highs in the low to mid 60s north of I-80 and upper 60s to 
around 70 south of I-80 keeping in mind actual values may verify plus
or minus a few degrees of our forecast.

Tonight looks quiet. Increasing upper-level cloud cover and 
continued onshore flow will hold overnight lows generally in the
mid to upper 50s, warmest near Lake Michigan and near US-24. 


Thursday into Friday: 

Ensemble model guidance remains in excellent agreement that the
southwestern US trough will eject northeastward and phase with 
a northern-stream trough screaming southeastward out of Canada. 
Am noting increasing agreement in the exact track and evolution 
of the resulting surface low, emerging from near Dodge City, KS 
Thursday morning to Kansas City, Missouri by early afternoon, 
passing directly over our area Thursday evening, and then 
continuing toward Southern Ontario overnight into Friday. 

As the surface low approaches on Thursday, gradually increasing
low-level isentropic ascent within the northward-moving 
baroclinic zone may support areas of drizzle and rain showers as
early as daybreak before a higher coverage of showers slides 
overhead during the afternoon and evening hours. Suppose there 
may be a thunderstorm or two as well, particularly Thursday 
evening as a narrow instability axis attempts to lift northward 
ahead of a southeastward-moving cold front. The severe weather 
threat continues to look very low for our area both from a 
conceptual model framework as well as from explicit output (of 
nearly zero probabilities) from ML-based guidance. With our area
smack-dab in the middle of the baroclinic zone, am anticipating
quite a gradient in high temperatures on Thursday. Will 
undercut NBM guidance and feature highs in the upper 50s near 
and north of I-88 and lower 60s south of I-80. Taken altogether,
Thursday looks fairly drab.

There remains agreement that an unusually strong surface high 
pressure system will quickly build into the central United 
States in the wake of the departing surface low leading to an 
impressive 40 to 45 mb pressure gradient directly over the Great
Lakes on Friday. A somewhat bifurcated pressure rise couplet (a
consequence of the upper-level troughs phasing directly 
overhead) suggest a one-two punch to winds on the backside of 
the system with a period of gusty northwesterly winds of 30 to 
35 mph Friday morning followed by a stronger period of gusts of 
35 to 40 mph during the afternoon and evening hours. Gusts may
be higher (locally 45 mph) along the Lake and Porter Indiana 
shorelines of Lake Michigan where lake instability will support 
deeper mixing profiles.
